The conference room of the Ministry of Energy in Cotonou served yesterday, Thursday 7 December 2017, as the setting for the signing of the implementation agreement of the Millennium Challenge Account-Benin II (MCA-Benin II) programme with the SBEE. The purpose of this agreement is to obtain the participation of the SBEE in carrying out the projects, and to make the programme's gains sustainable. "The MCA-Benin II programme must truly transform Benin's energy sector." This statement by Minister Houssou clearly shows the important role of energy for a country's development.

It was on the occasion of the signing of the implementation agreement of the MCA II programme with the Beninese Electric Energy Company (SBEE), yesterday Thursday 7 December 2017, that the minister expressed himself in these terms. The chosen venue: the premises of the Ministry of Energy in Cotonou. The objective pursued through this agreement is to obtain the effective participation of the SBEE in carrying out the projects, and to make the programme's gains sustainable for the benefit of all Beninese. Before the actual signing, the floor was given to speeches. For the resident director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), Christopher Broughton, this agreement falls within the framework of the grant between the MCC and the government of Benin.

"In accordance with this agreement, the SBEE has been identified as the implementing structure of Benin's second programme for the Millennium Challenge Account II," he indicated.

The SBEE's collaboration is indispensable to successfully carry out this programme, the Director General suggested. This is moreover what the national coordinator of MCA-Benin II, Gabriel Degbegni, thinks.

To achieve the set objectives

According to his explanations, in the context of carrying out the programme's activities, MCA-Benin II will be led to establish formal cooperative relations with various public and semi-public entities. According to him, these are partner structures indispensable to achieving the set objectives. Besides the SBEE, he added, MCA II will also sign agreements with the Electricity Regulatory Authority, the General Directorate of Energy, the Beninese Agency for Rural Electrification and Energy Management, the Electric Community of Benin, the Beninese Environment Agency and the town halls of the programme's intervention zones. "The implementation agreement therefore appears as a partnership contract between MCA-Benin II and these structures, in order to clearly define the obligations of each of the parties," he added. Explaining the rationale for this agreement, he stressed that it will make it possible to strengthen the SBEE's capacities in the programme's various areas of intervention, but also to make the projects' gains sustainable.

"I would like to count on the determination of each of the actors concerned for compliance with the obligations contained in this agreement," he hoped.

For his part, the Minister of Energy Jean-Claude Houssou observed that the second compact is a major asset for the energy sector, to be used wisely. According to his explanations, this agreement specifies the responsibilities incumbent on each party, and the SBEE must work tirelessly to achieve the objectives. Under this agreement, the SBEE will contribute to carrying out three of the four projects of the MCA-Benin II programme, which are: policy reforms and institutional strengthening, then electricity generation and distribution. MCA-Benin II, for its part, will have to manage the construction activities and ensure that they are properly and safely carried out.

a2899.t:
Le port Polyvalent de Doraleh à recu Dimanche 7 Aout 2022 le PDG de la Ethiopian Shipping Lines, Mr. Akawak Roba accompagne de hauts responsables de la Ethiopian Maritime & Transit Services (MTS). Par cette visite de courtoisie, les partenaires de DMP ont porté un message de félicitations à l’endroit du Directeur Général du Port Polyvalent de Doraleh M.Djama Ibrahim Darar et à toutes les équipes qui ont œuvrées au bon déroulement des opérations de logistiques portuaires et de transport.
Monsieur Roba a particulièrement félicité l’ensemble du personnel de DMP qui n’a ménagé aucun effort pour la manutention d’un volume de 1500 000 métrique / tonnes de vrac solide dans des temps records. Depuis l’annee 2019, un comité de suivi a été mis en place pour valider la stratégie à déployer pour la bonne coordination des activités de déchargement, de manutention, de stockage et de transport du cargo Ethiopien.
Une des démarches de cette stratégie mise en place cette saison a été de diversifier les moyens de transport car en plus du traditionnel corridor routier le DMP a déployé en partenariat avec la Ethiopian Djibouti Railway l’usage du train a marchandise : Le DMP TERMINAL RAILWAY. Notre terminal ferroviaire qui dispose de 5 voies ferrées a assuré la livraison de 65% de l’Engrais Ethiopien. Dans le domaine de l’aide humanitaire, il a été assuré la manutention et la livraison d’au moins 500 000 métriques tonnes de blé au cours de cette année. D’autres navires minéraliers sont prévus d’accoster au DMP d’ici la fin de l’année 2022. Aussitôt la saison finie, DMP a investi sur l’achat d’équipements supplémentaires de manutention pour renforcer la capacité opérationnelle du terminal vraquier. Le Port Polyvalent de Doraleh a clôturé la livraison de l’Engrais de cette saison 2021/2022 à temps pour la période des récoltes de l’Ethiopie.
Ceci, dans le souci d’accroitre les performances et d’augmenter les productivités de DMP qui ambitionne de devenir un leader incontesté parmi les Port Polyvalents régionaux et internationaux.
C’est avec fierté et un sens du devoir accompli qu’a été clôturée cette saison de l’Engrais Ethiopien. Mission accomplie pour cette année 2022.
a2899.en:
The Doraleh Multipurpose Port received on Sunday 7 August 2022 the CEO of Ethiopian Shipping Lines, Mr. Akawak Roba, accompanied by senior officials of Ethiopian Maritime & Transit Services (MTS). Through this courtesy visit, DMP's partners conveyed a message of congratulations to the Director General of the Doraleh Multipurpose Port, Mr. Djama Ibrahim Darar, and to all the teams that worked for the smooth running of port logistics and transport operations.
Mr. Roba particularly congratulated all of DMP's staff, who spared no effort in handling a volume of 1,500,000 metric tonnes of dry bulk in record time. Since 2019, a monitoring committee has been set up to validate the strategy to be deployed for the proper coordination of the unloading, handling, storage and transport activities for Ethiopian cargo.
One of the steps of this strategy put in place this season was to diversify the means of transport, because in addition to the traditional road corridor, DMP deployed, in partnership with the Ethiopian Djibouti Railway, the use of the freight train: the DMP TERMINAL RAILWAY. Our rail terminal, which has 5 tracks, ensured the delivery of 65% of the Ethiopian fertiliser. In the area of humanitarian aid, the handling and delivery of at least 500,000 metric tonnes of wheat was ensured during this year. Other bulk ore carriers are expected to dock at DMP by the end of 2022. As soon as the season ended, DMP invested in the purchase of additional handling equipment to strengthen the operational capacity of the bulk terminal. The Doraleh Multipurpose Port closed the delivery of this 2021/2022 season's fertiliser in time for Ethiopia's harvest period.
This is done with a view to increasing DMP's performance and productivity, as it aspires to become an undisputed leader among regional and international multipurpose ports.
It is with pride and a sense of duty accomplished that this Ethiopian Fertiliser season was closed. Mission accomplished for this year 2022.

a3026.t:
Amidst heightened political tension with France, Algeria has banned all French aid to private schools in the country.
An Algerian media outlet, TSA, reported on Monday that the government has directed private schools to stop accepting financial or other support from France.
For years, schools in Algeria have received development funding from France as part of France’s efforts to promote the French language and culture abroad.
This is a common practice in former French colonies, where France provided financial aid, teacher training, and educational materials to schools that taught in French or followed the French curriculum. Both public and private schools have received aid. It has also funded scholarships for Algerian students studying in France.
For instance, in 2022, France allocated €132 million to Algeria as official development assistance. Then, in February 2025, it set aside €121 million for scholarships for Algerian students in France.
France has always provided funding for scholarships, scientific research, and cooperation programs through the French Embassy and the French Institute in Algeria.
Suspension of French curriculum
However, due to the growing dispute between both countries, the Algerian government has begun suspending the decades-long arrangement.
In October 2023, the government ordered private schools to suspend the use of the French curriculum and teach only in Algerian national curriculum.
Before then, private schools in Algeria followed the French curriculum and even prepared students for French exams. However, Algeria’s authorities argued that just as Algerian schools cannot teach their curriculum abroad without agreements, foreign curriculums shouldn’t be taught in Algeria’s schools unless officially approved.
The government has also begun introducing English as a language in primary schools. Previously, French had been the only foreign language taught in schools.
Meanwhile, Algeria’s decision to stop development aid to private schools is also considered a response to the call from France’s right wing to suspend funding to the country.
Impact on diplomatic ties
This new directive is likely to distance Algeria from France and increase tension between them. It also further weakens France’s soft power in Africa and among its former colonies.
Although issues from their colonial past caused the prolonged dispute between the countries, the contention heightened after French President Emmanuel Macron shifted France’s position by recognising Morocco’s autonomy plan for Western Sahara as the “only basis” for resolving the conflict.
The Western Sahara is a disputed territory in North Africa, located between Morocco, Mauritania, and Algeria.
Morocco’s autonomy plan proposes that Western Sahara remain under Moroccan sovereignty but have some self-rule, allowing local governance while Morocco retains ultimate authority.
By backing Morocco’s claim over the region, France angered Algeria, which has always supported the Sahrawi people’s right to decide their future.
In November 2024, Algeria responded by instructing banks to suspend financial transactions with French companies – a move that disrupted trade between the two nations.
Also, the tension was worsened by Algeria’s refusal to accept the return of undocumented Algerian migrants from France on the grounds that their deportation was illegal.

a3152.t:
Pressure from U.S. aid freezes and global trade tension is unlikely to result in widescale credit downgrades in Africa, Fitch Ratings said on Thursday.
The impact of tariffs on Africa is limited, Fitch said, due to the region’s export composition and weaker integration into global supply chains compared to a region such as Asia.
But Sub-Saharan Africa has been one of the largest recipients of funds disbursed by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) which was frozen by executive order of U.S. President Donald Trump.
Nonetheless, South Africa, Namibia and Ivory Coast remain relatively shielded from recent events, Paul Gamble, head of Middle East/Africa in Fitch’s Sovereign Ratings Group, said.
And Nigeria and the Seychelles both hold positive credit outlooks from Fitch Ratings – an indication that a rating is expected to be raised in the future – thanks to ongoing reforms, he told a webinar.
“The reforms that we’ve seen really put the region in a better position to absorb some of these shocks,” Gamble.
“The impact for the ratings looks manageable.”
However, the freeze on U.S. foreign aid was not without negative consequences, Fitch said.
Some of the poorest nations were at risk for having projects come to an abrupt end and would see fiscal stability come under pressure. Ethiopia received U.S. assistance worth around 80% of its foreign exchange reserves, with Mozambique, Uganda, and Lesotho also seen at risk.
“African-owned multilateral banks might become more important institutions in this shifting landscape,” Arnaud Louis, senior director at Fitch, said on the webinar.
Gamble also pointed to Washington’s pivot to strategic investments in minerals in Africa as potentially becoming a new sphere for the trade tensions as it could intensify competition on the continent with China.
“Africa will be a playing field for U.S.-China tensions,” said Gamble. The U.S. interest is becoming “more opportunistic, transactional” focusing on access to minerals and rare earths rather than broad-based development, he said.
The Trump administration has said it wants to invest billions of dollars in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Congo’s minerals, which are used in mobile phones and electric cars, are currently dominated by China and its mining companies.

a3292.t:
The National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA) has reassured Nigerians, particularly Persons Living With HIV (PLWHIV), that the country has a steady supply of antiretroviral drugs and that HIV treatment services remain uninterrupted.
This is in response to concerns raised by the World Health Organisation (WHO) that Nigeria and seven other countries could face shortages of life-saving HIV medication due to the United States’ pause on foreign aid.
The Director-General of NACA, Temitope Ilori, in a statement issued on Wednesday, noted that the federal government has taken proactive measures to prevent any disruption in HIV treatment services.
Ms Ilori emphasised that the government has recently made some key financial commitments to cushion the impact of the US government’s aid pause and close the immediate funding gap.
“The Federal Executive Council (FEC) approved $1.07 Billion to finance the healthcare sector reforms under the Human Capital Opportunities for Prosperity and Equity (HOPE) programme, and also approved N4.8 billion for HIV treatment, while the Nigerian Senate also recently allocated an additional N300 billion to the health sector in the 2025 budget,” she said.
“These allocations are part of the government’s efforts to cushion the impact of the US government’s aid pause and close the immediate funding gap.”
The government has also earmarked N700 billion to combat HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria while also enhancing immunisation efforts nationwide.
Ms Ilori noted that these financial commitments are also part of a broader strategy to strengthen Nigeria’s health system, ensuring that essential services such as HIV treatment, testing, and prevention remain uninterrupted.
“We want to assure Nigerians, particularly those living with HIV, that there is no shortage of drugs and consumables and no immediate stop of services for HIV treatment, testing, and prevention in Nigeria,” she said.
She said all treatment centres and pharmacies will continue to have sufficient antiretroviral drugs, ensuring uninterrupted access to care.
WHO’s warning
The WHO had warned that disruptions caused by the US foreign aid suspension could reverse two decades of progress in the global fight against HIV, potentially leading to over 10 million new HIV infections and three million related deaths globally.
The global health body also warned that countries such as Haiti, Kenya, Lesotho, South Sudan, Burkina Faso, Mali, Nigeria, and Ukraine could face HIV drug shortages.
PEPFAR, the US President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief, which has funded HIV treatment for millions worldwide—including in Nigeria—faced temporary funding suspension following an executive order issued by President Donald Trump in January.
About two million Nigerians are currently living with HIV, with many of them benefitting from PEPFAR.
As one of the countries with the highest HIV burden globally, Nigeria relies heavily on programmes such as PEPFAR for access to life-saving medications and healthcare infrastructure support.
Over the years, PEPFAR has contributed over $6 billion to support Nigeria’s national HIV/AIDS response.
Closing the gap
While acknowledging the US government’s and its partners’ significant contributions over the past two decades, Ms Ilori said Nigeria views this funding gap as an opportunity to take ownership of its HIV response and strengthen local solutions.
She added that this is a crucial moment for the country to mobilise resources and ensure the sustainability of its HIV programme.
She reaffirmed NACA’s commitment to achieving HIV epidemic control in Nigeria and encouraged the public to rely on credible sources for updates regarding the country’s HIV response.

a3531.t:
Courant du mois de mars 2025 dans la ville de Denver dans l’État du Colorado, l’ex-candidat de gauche à la présidentielle de 2016 aux USA, Bernie Sanders, en campagne sur le thème « fighting oligarchy » a tenu un discours devant plus de 90.000 auditeurs qui mérite d’être porté à la connaissance de l’opinion publique africaine. En effet, une certaine intelligentsia béatement américanophile s’est spécialisée dans l’adulation de « la plus grande démocratie du monde » (sic!). Cette adoration de « l’american way of life » USA est devenue de nos jours un substitut à l’adoration longtemps entretenue du « modèle démocratique » que représentaient les métropoles coloniales françafricaines et eurafricaines.
Cette contagion touche même la frange de l’intelligentsia islamo-arabisante de nos pays qui se taisent sur les monarchies dictatoriales fascistes des pétro-dollars tout en étant attirée par les mirages prétendument développementaux que sont Dubaï, Doha, Singapour, Malaisie. Ce faisant, ceci rappelle l’adulation économiciste suscitée par la propagande anticommuniste impérialiste des années 70/80 pour les « Nouveaux Pays Industrialisés » (NPI) qu’étaient la Corée du Sud, Hong Kong, Taïwan qui maquillait les dictatures fascistes qui y régnaient.
Ces illusions d’optiques sont des leurres de la « mondialisation » libérale impérialiste sous hégémonie US dont la bulle éclate aujourd’hui sous nos yeux. En effet, quand on sépare l’essence de l’apparent, malgré quelques réussites industriels, ces mirages économiques que l’on brandit allègrement comme « modèles » pour le Sénégal et l’Afrique, sont en réalité des marchés Sandaga, donc des centres commerciaux financiarisés qui ne produisent quasiment rien mais vendent tout simplement les marchandises produites sous d’autres cieux. Adorer la dictature de l’argent qui fait et défait les gouvernements selon les intérêts des riches milliardaires fait partie des miroirs aux alouettes de la division internationale du travail entre pays dominants, oppresseurs et pays dominés, opprimés que l’avènement progressif du monde multipolaire anti-hégémonique démasque de plus en plus nettement.
Le doigt accusateur de Franz Fanon dans « Peau noire, masque blanc » prend aujourd’hui la forme de l’idolâtrie de « modèles » politico-économiques modélisés par la dictature hégémonique de la mondialisation libéralo-fasciste de l’impérialisme Otano/US/UE/G7/Israël. C’est cet avilissement mental, en plus du fatal sentiment d’impuissance, qui était à la base de l’engouement d’une certaine intelligentsia pour l’élection de « Obama, premier président noir des USA », ce qui montrait à souhait cette vassalisation intellectuelle occidentophile. L’élection comme président du commerçant mafieux Trump et ses annonces fracassantes de suppression des subventions de l’USAID, de sanctions généralisées pour imposer l’hégémonie US, notamment contre l’Afrique du Sud pour avoir pris des mesures de redistribution relative des terres en enfonçant un coin dans l’apartheid agraire, etc.
Les morceaux choisis ci-dessous du discours de Bernie Sanders remettent les pendules à l’heure sur les dessous cachés socio-économiques du modèle prétendument démocratique Étasunien.
Les USA, c’est la dictature de classe des milliardaires (ploutocratie)
« Le peuple américain, surtout avec M. Musk et les 13 milliardaires de l'administration Trump qui dirigent agence après agence…Ayant parcouru le pays, je peux vous dire que le peuple américain en a assez de ces inégalités et qu'il veut une économie qui profite à tous, et pas seulement aux 1% les plus riches… Le 1% le plus riche de notre pays possède désormais plus de richesses que les 90% les plus pauvres. Les PDG gagnent 300 fois plus que leur salarié moyen. Et aussi incroyable que cela puisse paraître – compte tenu de l'inflation réelle actuelle – le travailleur américain moyen, malgré une augmentation massive de la productivité, est aujourd'hui plus bas qu'il y a 52 ans. Et pendant cette période, 75.000 milliards de dollars de richesse ont été transférés des 90% les plus pauvres vers le 1% les plus riches... trois sociétés de Wall Street – BlackRock, Vanguard et State Street – sont, ensemble, les principaux actionnaires de 95% de nos entreprises. Vous avez compris ? Trois sociétés de Wall Street – trois – sont les principaux actionnaires de 95% des entreprises américaines… la pire forme d'addiction à laquelle ce pays est actuellement confronté est l'avidité de l'oligarchie ».
Les USA, c’est la misère toujours plus grande pour les travailleurs
« Et dans cette autre Amérique, 60% de notre population vit au jour le jour. Et des millions de travailleurs d'un bout à l'autre du pays tentent de survivre avec des salaires de misère… Contrairement à Donald Trump, j'ai grandi dans une famille qui vivait au jour le jour. Je connais les angoisses de mes parents, qui vivaient dans un appartement à loyer modéré. Avons-nous les moyens d'acheter ceci ? Pourquoi avez-vous acheté cela ? Et c'est le cas partout en Amérique. Que signifie vivre au jour le jour ? Cela signifie que chaque jour, des millions d'Américains s'inquiètent de la façon dont ils vont payer leur loyer ou leur prêt immobilier. Partout dans le pays, les loyers montent en flèche. Et les gens se demandent : que se passera-t-il, pour moi et mes enfants, si le loyer augmente de 20% et que je n'en ai pas les moyens ? Où vais-je vivre ? Dois-je retirer mon enfant de l'école ? Où vais-je le mettre ? Dans le pire des cas, est-ce que je vis dans ma voiture ? Soyons clairs. De nombreuses personnes qui travaillent aujourd'hui vivent à l'arrière de leur voiture… Je mets quiconque dans ce pays au défi – et encore moins une personne âgée, qui a besoin de soins de santé, qui a besoin de chauffer sa maison – d'essayer de survivre avec 15 000 dollars par an… Dans mon État, le coût des soins de santé augmente de 10 à 15%. Aux États-Unis, aujourd'hui, 85 millions de personnes sont sans assurance ou sous-assurées. Aujourd'hui, le système de santé n'a pas pour fonction de faire ce que ferait une société saine : garantir des soins de santé à tous de manière rentable... Comme chacun le sait, notre système de santé a pour fonction de générer des milliards de dollars de profits pour les compagnies d'assurance et les laboratoires pharmaceutiques… Nous sommes le pays le plus riche du monde : 800.000 personnes dorment dans la rue et 20 millions de personnes dépensent plus de 50% de leurs maigres revenus pour se loger. Imaginez-vous ? Vous travaillez et vous dépensez 50% de vos revenus pour vous loger ».
Les USA, c’est après l’esclavage, l’apartheid puis le racisme d’État
Le sceau de naissance des USA est le « white supremacy » qui s’est soldé par le génocide des Amérindiens, l’esclavage des Noirs et la discrimination des Hispaniques. Le capitalisme US a combiné l’exploitation de classe des actionnaires bourgeois sur tous les travailleurs de ce pays et la ségrégation raciale, culturelle, religieuse des minorités nationales pour diviser et régner. La politique étrangère US instrumentalise sa guerre anti-coloniale d’indépendance de la fin du 18éme siècle et sa guerre prétendument anti-esclavagiste contre la sécession des États du Sud de la seconde moitié du 19éme siècle pour vendre le narratif manipulateur de « l’american way of life » dont la marque de fabrique est l’esprit cow-boy qui allie « la loi du pistolet et l’avidité de l’or ».
Les luttes de libérations nationales des minorités noires ont été définies comme « mouvement des droits civiques » pour masquer leur véritable contenu anti-apartheid symbolisé par Rosa Park occupant le siège attribué au white dans les bus. Les suprémacistes Whites Étasuniens considèrent que « Les multiculturalistes américains rejettent l'héritage culturel de leur pays. Ils [...] souhaitent créer un pays aux civilisations multiples, c'est-à-dire un pays n'appartenant à aucune civilisation et dépourvu d'unité culturelle. L'histoire nous apprend qu'aucun État ainsi constitué n'a jamais perduré en tant que société cohérente » (Samuel P. Huntington). C’est cette idéologie suprémaciste racialiste, culturaliste interne qui a fondé les États-Unis que le capitalisme impérialiste US hégémonique projette sur le monde entier en tant que vision ataviquement inégalitaire entre les peuples, les nations, les pays, les États.
Les USA, c’est la fascisation et la guerre pour sauver son hégémonie sur le monde
Ayant été le bénéficiaire de la victoire de l’URSS et des peuples contre le projet génocidaire fasciste des Nazis allemands et de l’empire militariste japonais, l’impérialisme US, ayant perdu 500.000 soldats sans que son territoire ne soit touché alors que le peuple Soviétique en perdait 26 millions et 7000 villes détruites, s’est d’abord érigé en puissance tutélaire du monde capitaliste et ensuite après la défaite de l’URSS en puissance hégémonique mondiale en se lançant dans un cycle de guerres d’agression pour détruire les États, leur souveraineté et les recoloniser. C’est fut les cas de l’Irak, de la Yougoslavie, de l’Afghanistan, de la Libye, de la Syrie, etc avant procéder à des guerres par procuration de l’OTAN dans le Sahel, en Ukraine, de l’Arabie Saoudite contre le Yémen, d’Israël contre la Palestine, le Liban, du Rwanda contre la RDC par M23 interposé, etc.
Ces guerres directes et indirectes de l’impérialisme US flanqués de ses vassaux de l’UE/G7 se sont soldées par des résistances des peuples victimes ayant empêché les résultats escomptés par les prédateurs, à savoir le contrôle des sources de matières premières stratégiques pour rendre dépendant d’eux le développement en cours des pays émergents, notamment ceux des BRICS et du « consensus de Shanghai » qui prônent un monde multipolaire dans le respect des souverainetés nationales et des « coopérations bilatérales et multilatérales ‘gagnant-gagnant’ ».
Cet échec de plus en plus patent du projet de maintenir la domination unilatérale US flanquée de l’UE/G7/OTAN/Israël est un des facteurs explicatifs de l’avènement du phénomène Trump. Les « néocons » guerriers des Bush, Clinton, Obama, Biden se sont peu à peu trouvés confrontés à l’inexorable ascension socio-économique, scientifique, technologique, culturel de la Chine populaire communiste et au rejet de la poursuite de la vassalisation de l’URSS sous le renégat Gorbatchev et de la Russie sous le bourgeois compradore Eltsine par l’arrivée au pouvoir de la fraction souverainiste de la bourgeoisie Russe. La guerre par procuration de l’OTAN en Ukraine contre la Russie s’embourbe ainsi dans une défaite flagrante des va-t-en-guerre européens libéraux et sociaux-démocrates libéraux.
Trump représente politiquement les capitalistes de la côte ouest pacifique, ceux de la Silicon-Valley en contradiction avec les capitalistes de l’est, ceux de la côte est atlantique, dont la préoccupation centrale est comment stopper le développement stratégique de la Chine communiste. Il faut donc chercher à rompre les liens stratégiques entre Chine communiste et Russie bourgeoise ou tout au moins neutraliser la Russie bourgeoise pour concentrer toutes les forces du capitalisme impérialiste US contre le communisme chinois. Il faut aussi que les alliés-vassaux de l’UE/G7 payent pour soutenir le projet vain de sauvetage de l’hégémonie US sur le monde.
Telle la réorientation politique impulsée par Trump qui procède ainsi à coups de sanctions pour obtenir ce qu’il veut et d’intentions de prises de possessions comme le Panama, le Groenland, le Canada, les terres rares d’Ukraine, etc. Parions que toute cette agitation fébrile finira par un échec patent et qui ne fera qu’accroître le danger d’une troisième guerre mondiale.
En finir avec la servilité mentale néocoloniale pour libérer le Sénégal et l’Afrique
L’Afrique aux Africains, plus précisément aux peuples africains, c’est œuvrer à élaborer une théorie donc un programme révolutionnaire guidant la pratique des forces (classes) sociales africaines qui ont un intérêt conséquent à la libération nationale, panafricaine et l’émancipation sociale de l’Afrique. Ceux et celles qui se font chantres de la nécessité que « l’Afrique se pense en Africain », que « l’Africain cesse de penser avec les idéologies étrangères » passent parfois leur temps à singer ces curieuses « démocraties étrangères » capitalistes US ou Européenne corrompues. Ils nous invitent à rejeter « toute idéologie parce que l’idéologie n’est pas africaine » (sic!), ils refusent de regarder objectivement nos sociétés composées de classes sociales, ce que l’information selon laquelle sur les 65 morts recensées par Collectif CartograFreeSenegal dont 81% par balles lors de la bataille contre l’État hors la loi APR/BBY, 46,5% d’ouvriers mécaniciens, 27,5% d’élèves et étudiants et 12% de commerçants, probablement du secteur informel.
Toutes les classes sociales – petite bourgeoisie intellectuelle, bourgeoisie nationaliste, paysans, pêcheurs, éleveurs, travailleurs de l’informel, ouvriers – qui s’opposent à la domination néocoloniale impérialiste n’ont pas toutes la même lecture de la souveraineté nationale et panafricaine et les mêmes objectifs à long terme, mais toutes ont un intérêt conjoncturel aujourd’hui à s’unir sous l’égide politique de la petite bourgeoisie intellectuelle radicalement souverainiste.
C’est cette réalité qui s’impose de fait au Sénégal où la résistance du peuple a rencontré l’offre politique crédible de Pastef les Patriotes mais aussi au Mali, au Burkina, au Niger où l’inexistence d’une offre politique crédible a été remplacée par le pouvoir de la fraction souverainiste des armées nationales qui a découvert sur le terrain de la lutte contre l’insécurité djihado-terroriste, le séparatisme et le double jeu des impérialistes la nécessité de la souveraineté nationale.
Bien entendu, ces expériences souverainistes en cours ont leurs points forts et points faibles, mais elles doivent absolument se prolonger le plus possible dans l’accomplissement des tâches d’ancrage de la souveraineté nationale et panafricaine dans les peuples respectifs. Mobiliser dans l’action et la réflexion toutes les forces vives souverainistes au sein du peuple est la voie sûre du renouvellement par le dépassement de la classe politique actuellement dominée par les politiciens néocoloniaux de droite et de gauche. Il nous faut une pédagogie de l’unité, critique, unité au sein même du camp souverainiste tant au Sénégal, au Mali, au Burkina, au Niger en séparant clairement les valets libéraux néocoloniaux de droite et de gauche des courants qui traversent notre camp souverainiste.
Les classes et partis politiques néocoloniaux, y compris les ex-gauches, ont, par leur trahison éhontée des valeurs souverainistes professées d’antan, intérêts que les expériences souverainistes de cette seconde phase de libération nationale panafricaine échouent. La plupart de ces partis traîtres à la cause indépendantiste africaine n’ont aucun crédit auprès des masses, mais ils représentent des classes sociales, la petite bourgeoisie, la bourgeoisie, la féodalité, qui ont intérêt dans le système néocolonial et dans la mondialisation capitaliste libérale. C’est cela qui constitue le danger d’un retour en arrière réactionnaire tant que les racines économiques du néocolonialisme ne sont pas déracinées.
C’est aussi là que gît la nécessité de briser l’échine à ce cheval de Troie mental que constitue l’influence délétère de l’adoration béate des prétendues « grandes démocraties » que seraient les USA aujourd’hui et qu’étaient les puissances colonisatrices Européennes hier.
Ouvrons des débats sérieux sur ces problématiques qui existent au sein même du camp souverainiste.
Diagne Fodé roland 
04/03/25
a3531.en:
In the course of March 2025, in the city of Denver in the State of Colorado, the former left-wing candidate in the 2016 US presidential election, Bernie Sanders, campaigning on the theme "fighting oligarchy", gave a speech before more than 90,000 listeners that deserves to be brought to the attention of African public opinion. Indeed, a certain blissfully America-loving intelligentsia has specialised in the adulation of "the greatest democracy in the world" (sic!). This adoration of the "American way of life" of the USA has today become a substitute for the long-cultivated adoration of the "democratic model" represented by the Francafrican and Eurafrican colonial metropoles.

This contagion even affects the Islamo-Arabising fringe of our countries' intelligentsia, who keep silent about the fascist dictatorial petrodollar monarchies while being attracted by the supposedly developmental mirages that are Dubai, Doha, Singapore and Malaysia. In so doing, this recalls the economistic adulation aroused by imperialist anti-communist propaganda in the 1970s and 1980s for the "Newly Industrialised Countries" (NICs) that were South Korea, Hong Kong and Taiwan, which disguised the fascist dictatorships that reigned there.

These optical illusions are the lures of imperialist liberal "globalisation" under US hegemony, whose bubble is bursting today before our eyes. Indeed, when one separates the essence from the appearance, despite a few industrial successes, these economic mirages that are cheerfully brandished as "models" for Senegal and Africa are in reality Sandaga markets, that is to say financialised shopping centres that produce practically nothing but simply sell the goods produced under other skies. Worshipping the dictatorship of money, which makes and unmakes governments according to the interests of rich billionaires, is part of the decoys of the international division of labour between dominant, oppressor countries and dominated, oppressed countries - a division that the gradual advent of an anti-hegemonic multipolar world is unmasking ever more clearly.

Frantz Fanon's accusing finger in "Black Skin, White Masks" takes today the form of the idolatry of politico-economic "models" modelled by the hegemonic dictatorship of the liberal-fascist globalisation of NATO/US/EU/G7/Israeli imperialism. It is this mental debasement, in addition to the fatal feeling of powerlessness, that was at the root of a certain intelligentsia's enthusiasm for the election of "Obama, the first black president of the USA", which amply demonstrated this Western-loving intellectual vassalisation. The election as president of the mafia-like trader Trump and his thunderous announcements of the elimination of USAID subsidies, of generalised sanctions to impose US hegemony, notably against South Africa for having taken measures of relative land redistribution driving a wedge into agrarian apartheid, etc.

The selected excerpts below from Bernie Sanders' speech set the record straight on the hidden socio-economic underside of the supposedly democratic US model.

The USA is the class dictatorship of billionaires (plutocracy)

"The American people, especially with Mr Musk and the 13 billionaires in the Trump administration running agency after agency... Having travelled the country, I can tell you that the American people are fed up with this inequality and that they want an economy that benefits everyone, and not just the richest 1%... The richest 1% of our country now owns more wealth than the poorest 90%. CEOs earn 300 times more than their average employee. And as incredible as it may seem - given actual current inflation - the average American worker, despite a massive increase in productivity, is today lower than 52 years ago. And during that period, 75 trillion dollars of wealth have been transferred from the poorest 90% to the richest 1%... three Wall Street firms - BlackRock, Vanguard and State Street - are, together, the principal shareholders of 95% of our companies. Do you understand? Three Wall Street firms - three - are the principal shareholders of 95% of American companies... the worst form of addiction this country currently faces is the greed of the oligarchy."

The USA means ever greater misery for workers

"And in that other America, 60% of our population lives from day to day [paycheck to paycheck]. And millions of workers from one end of the country to the other are trying to survive on miserable wages... Unlike Donald Trump, I grew up in a family that lived paycheck to paycheck. I know the anxieties of my parents, who lived in a rent-controlled apartment. Can we afford to buy this? Why did you buy that? And that is the case all over America. What does it mean to live paycheck to paycheck? It means that every day, millions of Americans worry about how they are going to pay their rent or their mortgage. All over the country, rents are soaring. And people ask themselves: what will happen, for me and my children, if the rent goes up by 20% and I cannot afford it? Where am I going to live? Must I take my child out of school? Where am I going to put him? In the worst case, do I live in my car? Let us be clear. Many people who work today live in the back of their car... I challenge anyone in this country - let alone an elderly person, who needs health care, who needs to heat their home - to try to survive on 15,000 dollars a year... In my state, the cost of health care is rising by 10 to 15%. In the United States today, 85 million people are uninsured or under-insured. Today, the health system does not have the function of doing what a healthy society would do: guaranteeing health care for all in a cost-effective way... As everyone knows, our health system has the function of generating billions of dollars of profits for the insurance companies and the pharmaceutical laboratories... We are the richest country in the world: 800,000 people sleep in the street and 20 million people spend more than 50% of their meagre incomes on housing. Can you imagine? You work and you spend 50% of your income on housing."

The USA is, after slavery and apartheid, state racism

The birth seal of the USA is "white supremacy", which resulted in the genocide of the Native Americans, the enslavement of Blacks and the discrimination against Hispanics. US capitalism combined the class exploitation by bourgeois shareholders of all the workers of this country with the racial, cultural and religious segregation of national minorities in order to divide and rule. US foreign policy instrumentalises its anti-colonial war of independence of the late 18th century and its supposedly anti-slavery war against the secession of the Southern states in the second half of the 19th century in order to sell the manipulative narrative of the "American way of life", whose trademark is the cowboy spirit that combines "the law of the pistol and the greed for gold".

The national liberation struggles of the black minorities were defined as a "civil rights movement" in order to mask their true anti-apartheid content, symbolised by Rosa Parks occupying the seat allocated to whites on buses. US white supremacists consider that "American multiculturalists reject their country's cultural heritage. They [...] wish to create a country of many civilisations, that is to say a country belonging to no civilisation and devoid of cultural unity. History teaches us that no state thus constituted has ever endured as a coherent society" (Samuel P. Huntington). It is this internal racialist, culturalist supremacist ideology that founded the United States which hegemonic US imperialist capitalism projects onto the whole world as an atavistically inegalitarian vision among peoples, nations, countries and states.

The USA means fascisation and war to save its hegemony over the world

Having been the beneficiary of the victory of the USSR and of the peoples against the genocidal fascist project of the German Nazis and of the Japanese militarist empire, US imperialism - having lost 500,000 soldiers without its territory being touched, while the Soviet people lost 26 million and 7,000 destroyed cities - first set itself up as the tutelary power of the capitalist world and then, after the defeat of the USSR, as the world hegemonic power, launching itself into a cycle of wars of aggression to destroy states, their sovereignty, and to recolonise them. That was the case of Iraq, Yugoslavia, Afghanistan, Libya, Syria, etc., before proceeding to proxy wars by NATO in the Sahel and in Ukraine, by Saudi Arabia against Yemen, by Israel against Palestine and Lebanon, by Rwanda against the DRC through the M23, etc.

These direct and indirect wars of US imperialism, flanked by its EU/G7 vassals, have resulted in resistance by the victim peoples that prevented the results expected by the predators, namely control of the sources of strategic raw materials in order to make the ongoing development of emerging countries dependent on them, notably those of the BRICS and of the "Shanghai consensus", which advocate a multipolar world respecting national sovereignties and "win-win bilateral and multilateral cooperation".

This increasingly evident failure of the project of maintaining unilateral US domination flanked by the EU/G7/NATO/Israel is one of the explanatory factors of the advent of the Trump phenomenon. The warmongering "neocons" of Bush, Clinton, Obama and Biden found themselves gradually confronted with the inexorable socio-economic, scientific, technological and cultural rise of communist People's China and with the rejection of the continued vassalisation of the USSR under the renegade Gorbachev and of Russia under the comprador bourgeois Yeltsin, through the coming to power of the sovereigntist faction of the Russian bourgeoisie. NATO's proxy war in Ukraine against Russia is thus bogging down in a flagrant defeat for the European liberal and liberal social-democratic warmongers.

Trump politically represents the capitalists of the Pacific west coast, those of Silicon Valley, in contradiction with the capitalists of the east, those of the Atlantic east coast, whose central preoccupation is how to stop the strategic development of communist China. It is therefore necessary to seek to break the strategic links between communist China and bourgeois Russia, or at the very least to neutralise bourgeois Russia in order to concentrate all the forces of US imperialist capitalism against Chinese communism. It is also necessary that the EU/G7 allies-vassals pay to support the vain project of saving US hegemony over the world.

Such is the political reorientation driven by Trump, who thus proceeds by means of sanctions to obtain what he wants and by intentions of taking possession, such as Panama, Greenland, Canada, the rare earths of Ukraine, etc. Let us wager that all this feverish agitation will end in obvious failure and will only increase the danger of a third world war.

Putting an end to neocolonial mental servility in order to liberate Senegal and Africa

Africa for the Africans, more precisely for the African peoples, means working to develop a theory and therefore a revolutionary programme guiding the practice of the African social forces (classes) that have a consequential interest in the national and pan-African liberation and the social emancipation of Africa. Those who make themselves champions of the necessity that "Africa think as an African", that "the African stop thinking with foreign ideologies", sometimes spend their time aping those curious corrupt US or European capitalist "foreign democracies". They invite us to reject "all ideology because ideology is not African" (sic!); they refuse to look objectively at our societies composed of social classes - as shown by the information that, of the 65 deaths recorded by the Collectif CartograFreeSenegal, 81% of them by gunfire during the battle against the outlaw APR/BBY state, 46.5% were mechanic workers, 27.5% pupils and students and 12% traders, probably from the informal sector.

All the social classes - the intellectual petty bourgeoisie, the nationalist bourgeoisie, peasants, fishermen, herders, informal-sector workers, labourers - that oppose imperialist neocolonial domination do not all have the same reading of national and pan-African sovereignty and the same long-term objectives, but all have a conjunctural interest today in uniting under the political aegis of the radically sovereigntist intellectual petty bourgeoisie.

It is this reality that imposes itself in fact in Senegal, where the people's resistance met the credible political offer of Pastef les Patriotes, but also in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, where the non-existence of a credible political offer was replaced by the power of the sovereigntist faction of the national armies, which discovered on the ground of the struggle against jihadi-terrorist insecurity, separatism and the double game of the imperialists the necessity of national sovereignty.

Of course, these ongoing sovereigntist experiences have their strong points and weak points, but they must absolutely be prolonged as much as possible in the accomplishment of the tasks of anchoring national and pan-African sovereignty in their respective peoples. Mobilising in action and reflection all the living sovereigntist forces within the people is the sure path to renewal through the surpassing of the political class currently dominated by neocolonial politicians of the right and of the left. We need a pedagogy of unity, criticism, unity within the sovereigntist camp itself, in Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, by clearly separating the neocolonial liberal lackeys of the right and of the left from the currents that run through our sovereigntist camp.

The neocolonial classes and political parties, including the former lefts, have - through their shameless betrayal of the sovereigntist values they professed in the past - an interest in the failure of the sovereigntist experiences of this second phase of pan-African national liberation. Most of these parties that betray the African independence cause have no credit with the masses, but they represent social classes - the petty bourgeoisie, the bourgeoisie, the feudality - that have an interest in the neocolonial system and in liberal capitalist globalisation. That is what constitutes the danger of a reactionary step backwards as long as the economic roots of neocolonialism are not uprooted.

That is also where lies the necessity of breaking the back of that mental Trojan horse constituted by the deleterious influence of the blissful adoration of the supposedly "great democracies" that the USA is said to be today and that the European colonising powers were yesterday.

Let us open serious debates on these problems that exist within the sovereigntist camp itself.

Diagne Fode Roland
04/03/25

Adam Ibrahim was working with the UN humanitarian agency, OCHA, in his home country, Sudan, when conflict between rival armed forces erupted in early 2023 and he became a refugee alongside thousands of others who continue to flee the ongoing violence.
Sudan is one of the world’s largest and most complex humanitarian crises, with more than 30.4 million people – over half the population – urgently needing humanitarian assistance, yet the 2025 Sudan humanitarian needs and response plan is severely underfunded, with only 13.3 per cent of the required resources received so far.
Forced to flee the country with his family after the war intensified, Mr. Ibrahim returned to help people affected by the war in Darfur. Ahead of World Humanitarian Day, marked annually on 19 August, he described his journey, from aid worker to refugee and back again to Sudan.
“I was at home helping my daughter revise for her grade six exams, scheduled for the next day. Then, out of nowhere, the sound of heavy gunfire shattered the silence in my hometown, Zalingei, the capital of Central Darfur state, which remains gripped by insecurity and critical shortages of basic services.
At first, I thought the gunfire would pass quickly. I rushed to stock up on food supplies and water, enough for six days. But, the streets became battlegrounds. All I could do was try to keep my family safe.
Despite the chaos, I continued to work. Electricity and Internet access were sporadic, but I kept my phone charged to send daily updates to the OCHA Head of Office. It gave me purpose amid the uncertainty.
Eventually, it became too dangerous to stay.
The journey of displacement
On the 39th day, we fled. Our family of 10 began a harrowing journey with no clear destination, only the desperate need to escape. We left behind more than just walls and belongings; we left behind a life built with love and hope.
Our journey took us first to Nyala in South Darfur, then to Kosti in White Nile State. From there, we crossed the border into neighbouring South Sudan and eventually reached Uganda, a country I had heard offered stability and a good education system for children. The journey by car took 23 days. My children had no passports, and there were no refugee camps for Sudanese nationals at the time.
To my relief, migration authorities in both countries were kind and supportive. In Kampala, we rented a house and received asylum status within three days. The moment I held our refugee cards, I exhaled deeply and thought ‘we’ve made it.’
I enrolled my children in school and began working online, finally finding a sense of stability.
Here I was, an aid worker now a refugee, needing the same support I once provided to others.
Returning to Zalingei
Months later, I faced a difficult decision. Do I stay with my family or return to Darfur and continue the work I had done for years? I chose to return.
Leaving my family behind was incredibly hard, but their safety was paramount.
I returned to Zalingei with a renewed sense of duty to serve those still trapped in the hardship I had endured. I was also the sole breadwinner for my family and needed to ensure they could survive in Uganda.
My hometown changed
When I arrived in Zalingei, I barely recognised it. Buildings were scarred with bullet holes.
I found another family sheltering inside our house, a doctor and his family whose own home had been destroyed. I let them stay, setting aside a small section for myself and a colleague. The house had been looted. Windows were gone and our belongings had vanished. I had hoped to find my children’s school certificates, photos, any documents left behind. But, they were gone.
Everyone was armed, even children as young as 15. People were tense, traumatised and always bracing for the next wave of violence.
Machine guns and wreckage in West Darfur
I didn’t stay long in Zalingei. Soon I was called to El Geneina in West Darfur, a town devastated by violence, and whose people desperately needed humanitarian support.
El Geneina’s streets were strewn with the wreckage of burned-out military vehicles. Armed men patrolled in pickup trucks mounted with machine guns.
The humanitarian needs were immense. People lacked food, shelter, household essentials, healthcare, clean water and protection, but we never had enough resources for them.
Family, sacrifice and hope for Sudan
It’s heartbreaking to witness the suffering caused by the recent donor funding cuts. Many organizations have been forced to scale back their operations, leaving countless people without help.
Still, we did all we could.
Between 2023 and 2025, we reached more than 800,000 displaced people with critical assistance, in West and Central Darfur.
I also went on to work with OCHA colleagues in Chad to coordinate cross-border humanitarian convoys into Darfur.
These convoys were lifelines, delivering food, medicine and supplies to communities cut off by conflict.
Today, I remain in Sudan.
My family is still in Uganda. I visit them once a year, but the separation is painful.”
GIK/APA

a3733.t:
Présente avec une très forte délégation au championnat national scolaire, Aplahoué 2025, la direction technique nationale de la Fédération béninoise de volleyball avec sa tête le DTN, Franck Lokonon travaille à détecter des talents à polir pour le volley-ball béninois de demain.
Dans un entretien accordé à notre quotidien, le Directeur Technique National de la FBVB, Franck Lokonon explique la quintessence de sa direction sur la phase nationale du championnat scolaire qui se tient dans la ville d’Aplahoué depuis le samedi 21 Juin dernier, le niveau de jeu des jeunes volleyeurs, la collaboration de son service avec les experts internationaux recrutés par l’Etat ainsi que les actualités brûlantes du volley-ball béninois.
Matin Libre : Présentez-vous à nos lecteurs ?
Franck Lokonon : « Je m’appelle Franck Lokonon, Directeur Technique National de volleyball du Bénin. »
Pourquoi la présence de la DTN sur ce championnat ?
« La présence de la Direction Technique Nationale (DTN) sur ce championnat est vraiment primordiale parce que la pépinière au niveau du volleyball doit être vue et entretenue. Par conséquent, la DTN s’est faite pour mission d’accompagner les projets du gouvernement en accompagnant ce championnat scolaire. »
Après quatre journées de compétition, quelle est votre appréciation sur le niveau de jeu des apprenants ?
« Au niveau du jeu, je peux vous dire que les enfants ont un niveau très relevé. Le jeu est assis sur des techniques qui sont exécutées pour certains à la perfection et chez d’autres, il reste encore du boulot à faire. Mais je vous dis, sur les deux années de championnat scolaire que nous avons eues au volleyball, les encadrants ont vraiment fait progresser nos enfants et nous, en tant que techniciens, nous en sommes contents. Nous avons la chair de poule sur certains matchs où on voit de petits enfants qui se donnent et qui exécutent la touche, la manchette, la réception avec une intelligence de jeu qui donne envie aux grandes personnes de venir voir les matchs de volleyball. »
Nous avons constaté que depuis deux ans, le ministère a recruté certains experts internationaux pour donner un coup de pouce technique aux différentes fédérations sportives. Comment se passe la collaboration entre la DTN et les experts ?
« La collaboration se passe très bien entre les experts et la Direction Technique Nationale parce que la Direction Technique Nationale a ses démembrements qui sont les conseillers techniques régionaux et qui travaillent de concert avec les experts sur toutes les sélections, tous les regroupements et tout ce qu’il y a au niveau de chaque démembrement au niveau des experts. Je peux vous dire que le coup de pouce que la présence de ces experts, nous donne aujourd’hui au volleyball n’est pas négligeable. Il faudrait encourager et qu’on fasse tout pour tirer le meilleur de ces experts pour qu’après leur départ du Bénin, qu’on sache vraiment que des gens, des connaisseurs, des sachants ont pris part là et que leur génération sera une génération qui va briller au plan international. »
Quelle est la plus value de l’organisation des championnats scolaires pour les fédérations sportives ?
« Pour les fédérations, vous n’êtes pas sans savoir que tout le sport se repose sur le scolaire. Et quand ces scolaires vont grandir, ils viendront dans la vie civile. Et nous, Fédération, nous aurons le plaisir de les accueillir. Nous nous ferons le devoir de les entretenir pour que nos fédérations vivent réellement parce que sans la formation à la base que nous sommes en train de faire, il n’y aura pas le sommet. D’ici 10-15 ans, ceux qui sont actuellement là vont céder la place à ce que nous sommes en train de voir jouer très jeune aujourd’hui. »
Vous venez de parler de l’élite est-ce qu’on peut avoir quelques nouvelles du championnat national de la Fédération ?
« Je peux vous dire que nous sommes à la 13e journée du championnat actuellement et c’est les matchs retours. Nous sommes en train d’aller vers la fin de ces matchs de la phase retour pour passer à la phase regroupée des meilleurs et des moins bons pour pouvoir continuer la deuxième phase de notre championnat. Et je vous assure, à ces phases regroupées, vous allez voir encore du volleyball et du vrai volley. »
On a constaté que, ces derniers temps, le volley-ball s’exporte hors du pays, notamment dans les pays occidentaux. Comment se fait ce management ?
« Nous allons remercier notre président de la fédération qui fait tout pour faire briller notre volleyball sur le plan international. Je veux nommer monsieur Ali Yaro qui fait vraiment beaucoup sur le plan international pour faire briller notre volleyball parce qu’il a de ces relations qui permettent à d’autres de venir voir notre championnat et de venir prendre ceux qui peuvent nous représenter valablement. On a exporté plus d’un, on a des partenariats avec d’autres et on vous assure que ces petits que nous découvrons aujourd’hui passeront par là.»
La mauvaise note, c’est la non-participation de l’équipe championne féminine du Bénin Queen’s, à la dernière Ligue des champions au Nigeria. Quel appel avez-vous à lancer pour qu’on assiste plus à ces défections ?
Je peux vous dire que l’équipe de Queen’s Vbc n’a pas pu participer à la compétition de la zone 3 au Burkina Faso parce que l’équipe est en reconstruction. C’est une équipe qui se repose sur certaines joueuses de qualités physique, athlétique et technique très élevées entre-temps, qui aujourd’hui, ces talents se sont vus exporter et l’équipe de Queen’s Vbc est en train de reconstruire petit à petit son effectif pour garder le niveau. À un moment donné, l’équipe a vu qu’elle ne pourra pas représenter valablement le pays avec l’effectif qu’elle a actuellement et elle a pu décider de ne pas participer. Mais je vous assure, cette équipe reviendra toujours en force. Je remercie aussi, l’équipe de l’Énergie Vbc qui a fait très forte sensation dans ce championnat de la Coupe d’Afrique de la zone 3, qui est auréolée d’une médaillée d’agent. Vraiment, je remercie tous les cadres techniques qui ont pu œuvrer pour cette performance exceptionnelle afin qu’on puisse revenir avec cette médaille d’argent en attendait bien sûr l’or. D’ici deux ou trois ans, ne soyez pas surpris de nous voir en or au plan régional. »
Un mot pour conclure cet entretien
« C’est un mot que je ne sais pas dire. Je remercierai sincèrement tous les journalistes qui œuvrent pour la visibilité de notre sport, tous ceux qui, dans l’ombre, font pour que le sport puisse être vu à l’international. Je remercierai tous les cadres de la Direction technique nationale qui font tout pour aller toucher les plus petits dans les plus grands recoins du Bénin pour en faire des talents. Je remercierai aussi Monsieur le Président Ali Yaro pour tout ce qu’il fait pour le volley-ball béninois. Je n’oublierai pas le ministère qui a pensé à mettre à la disposition des fédérations sportives des cadres techniques, des cadres chevronnés pour la reconstitution du sport béninois. Merci. »
Jeraud LANGANFIN GLELE
a3733.en:
Present with a very large delegation at the national schools championship, Aplahoue 2025, the national technical directorate of the Beninese Volleyball Federation, headed by the DTN, Franck Lokonon, is working to detect talents to be polished for the Beninese volleyball of tomorrow.

In an interview granted to our daily, the National Technical Director of the FBVB, Franck Lokonon, explains the essence of his directorate's role at the national phase of the schools championship being held in the town of Aplahoue since Saturday 21 June, the level of play of the young volleyball players, his service's collaboration with the international experts recruited by the State, as well as the hot news of Beninese volleyball.

Matin Libre: Introduce yourself to our readers?
Franck Lokonon: "My name is Franck Lokonon, National Technical Director of volleyball of Benin."

Why is the DTN present at this championship?
"The presence of the National Technical Directorate (DTN) at this championship is really essential because the nursery at the volleyball level must be seen and maintained. Consequently, the DTN has made it its mission to support the government's projects by accompanying this schools championship."

After four days of competition, what is your assessment of the level of play of the pupils?
"In terms of play, I can tell you that the children have a very high level. The game rests on techniques that are executed, for some, to perfection, and for others, there is still work to be done. But I tell you, over the two years of the schools championship we have had in volleyball, the coaches have really made our children progress and we, as technicians, are happy about it. We get goosebumps at some matches where we see little children who give their all and who execute the set, the dig, the reception with a game intelligence that makes grown-ups want to come and watch volleyball matches."

We have noted that for two years the ministry has recruited certain international experts to give a technical boost to the various sports federations. How is the collaboration between the DTN and the experts going?
"The collaboration is going very well between the experts and the National Technical Directorate because the National Technical Directorate has its branches, which are the regional technical advisers, and who work hand in hand with the experts on all the selections, all the training camps and everything there is at the level of each branch at the level of the experts. I can tell you that the boost that the presence of these experts gives us today in volleyball is not negligible. We should encourage it and do everything to get the best out of these experts so that after their departure from Benin, we really know that people, connoisseurs, knowledgeable people took part there and that their generation will be a generation that will shine internationally."

What is the added value of organising the schools championships for the sports federations?
"For the federations, you are not unaware that all sport rests on schools. And when these pupils grow up, they will come into civilian life. And we, the Federation, will have the pleasure of welcoming them. We will make it our duty to maintain them so that our federations truly live, because without the grassroots training we are doing, there will be no summit. In 10-15 years, those who are currently there will give way to those we are now seeing play very young today."

You have just spoken of the elite — can we have some news of the Federation's national championship?
"I can tell you that we are currently at the 13th round of the championship and these are the return matches. We are heading towards the end of these return-phase matches in order to move to the grouped phase of the best and the less good so as to continue the second phase of our championship. And I assure you, at these grouped phases, you will again see volleyball and real volley."

We have noted that, lately, volleyball is being exported out of the country, notably to Western countries. How is this management done?
"We will thank our federation president who does everything to make our volleyball shine internationally. I want to name Mr Ali Yaro who really does a lot internationally to make our volleyball shine because he has those connections that allow others to come and see our championship and to come and take those who can validly represent us. We have exported more than one, we have partnerships with others and we assure you that these little ones we are discovering today will go through there."

The bad note is the non-participation of Benin's women's champion team, Queen's, in the last Champions League in Nigeria. What appeal do you have to make so that we no longer see such withdrawals?
"I can tell you that the Queen's VBC team could not take part in the Zone 3 competition in Burkina Faso because the team is being rebuilt. It is a team that rested on certain players of very high physical, athletic and technical quality in the meantime, who today have seen these talents exported, and the Queen's VBC team is rebuilding its squad little by little to keep the level. At a certain point, the team saw that it would not be able to validly represent the country with the squad it currently has and it was able to decide not to participate. But I assure you, this team will always come back in force. I also thank the Energie VBC team which made a very strong impression in this Zone 3 Africa Cup championship, which is crowned with a silver medal. Really, I thank all the technical staff who were able to work for this exceptional performance so that we could come back with this silver medal while awaiting of course gold. In two or three years, do not be surprised to see us in gold at the regional level."

A word to conclude this interview
"It is a word I do not know how to say. I would sincerely thank all the journalists who work for the visibility of our sport, all those who, in the shadows, work so that sport can be seen internationally. I would thank all the officials of the National Technical Directorate who do everything to go and reach the smallest children in the furthest corners of Benin to make talents of them. I would also thank Mr President Ali Yaro for everything he does for Beninese volleyball. I will not forget the ministry which thought to place at the disposal of the sports federations technical officials, seasoned officials, for the reconstitution of Beninese sport. Thank you."

Jeraud LANGANFIN GLELE

a3737.t: O Sucesso do Programa do governo para expansão de electricidade “Energia para Todos” foi destaque, esta quarta-feira, nas reuniões de Primavera do Banco Mundial e Fundo Monetário Internacional, que decorrem em Washington DC. O Ministro da Economia e Finanças de Moçambique foi convidado a explicar, num painel de debate, a razão por detrás do sucesso das politicas do governo. Na ocasião Max Tonela esclareceu que a abertura do executivo em cooperar com o sector privado foi um dos factores mais importantes para expansão da rede eléctrica no País.
a3737.en: The success of the government's programme for the expansion of electricity, "Energy for All," was highlighted on Wednesday at the Spring Meetings of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, being held in Washington DC. Mozambique's Minister of Economy and Finance was invited to explain, on a debate panel, the reason behind the success of the government's policies. On the occasion, Max Tonela explained that the executive's openness to cooperating with the private sector was one of the most important factors in the expansion of the electricity grid in the country.

a3747.t:
La Nation Bénin...
L’Agence américaine pour le développement international
(Usaid) a officiellement cessé d’exister, ce mardi 1er juillet, après plus de
six décennies d’engagement dans plus de 100 pays. En Afrique subsaharienne où
plusieurs pays dont le Bénin figuraient parmi les principaux bénéficiaires,
cette dissolution rebat les cartes de la coopération et se présente comme un
départ pour d’autres systèmes de financement innovants. 
C’est un véritable tournant dans l’histoire de la
coopération internationale. Ce mardi 1er juillet, l’Agence américaine pour le
développement international (Usaid), pilier de la diplomatie humanitaire
américaine depuis 1961, a été officiellement dissoute, conformément à une
décision prise en mars dernier par le Congrès américain et entérinée par la
Maison-Blanche. Cela marque la fin d’un modèle de l’aide au développement tel
qu’il s’est construit au XXe siècle. 
D’après les données de l’Organisation de coopération et
de développement économiques (Ocde), l’Afrique subsaharienne absorbait près de
40 % du budget annuel de l’Usaid. Des pays comme le Bénin, le Togo, le Burkina
Faso, le Sénégal ou encore le Nigeria figuraient parmi les principaux
bénéficiaires. Au Bénin, l’Usaid finançait des projets structurants pour
l’accès à l’eau potable, la lutte contre le paludisme et le renforcement des
systèmes de santé communautaire. Au Togo, Burkina Faso, Nigeria et Sénégal,
plusieurs programmes ont transformé le quotidien de milliers de petits
exploitants agricoles et contribué à l’électrification rurale. L’appui a permis
d’améliorer l’éducation des jeunes filles, la résilience climatique et la
gouvernance locale.
Selon la Maison-Blanche, les missions de l’Usaid seront
désormais intégrées directement au sein d’une Direction générale de la
coopération et du développement, rattachée au Département d’État américain.
Officiellement, il s’agit de rationaliser la structure, limiter les doublons
administratifs et renforcer l’alignement entre l’aide au développement et les
priorités diplomatiques des États-Unis. Mais cette réorganisation interroge sur
sa mise en œuvre concrète. 
Les ambassades américaines dans chaque pays devront
négocier de nouveaux accords de continuité avec les gouvernements et les
acteurs locaux, pour éviter une interruption brutale de services essentiels.
Des millions de personnes dans le monde bénéficiaient chaque année des programmes de l’Usaid, dont près d’un quart en Afrique de l’Ouest. La Banque mondiale rappelle que l’agence figurait parmi les cinq premiers bailleurs bilatéraux pour les Objectifs de développement durable (Odd) liés à la santé, à l’éducation et à l’égalité des genres. Dans la pratique, certaines conventions tripartites ont déjà été prolongées jusqu’en 2026, notamment dans les domaines jugés stratégiques comme la santé communautaire, l’éducation et la sécurité alimentaire. Si l’institution devrait reprendre les activités, la nouvelle direction générale pourrait mettre 12 à 18 mois pour devenir pleinement opérationnelle.
Motivations
Côté américain, la dissolution est présentée comme une
mesure de bonne gestion des deniers publics. Un rapport du Government
Accountability Office (Gao) souligne que l’Usaid gérait plus de 1 300 projets
dans 80 missions à l’étranger, avec parfois des doublons entre agences
fédérales. L’administration américaine défend un recentrage sur les priorités
diplomatiques majeures, dans un contexte de rivalité accrue avec la Chine sur
les investissements en Afrique et en Asie. Pourtant, plusieurs responsables
américains trouvent que la force de l’Usaid résidait précisément dans son
autonomie opérationnelle et son expertise technique. Selon eux, l’expertise
technique accumulée au fil des décennies par les équipes de l’Usaid pourrait
être diluée, voire perdue dans un ensemble diplomatique plus large où l’aide
risque de devenir un simple outil d’influence géopolitique. 
Après 63 ans d’existence, l’Usaid laisse derrière elle un héritage fait de succès, dont les actions sont appréciées par les populations. Sa dissolution marque la fin d’un modèle, au moment où la coopération internationale doit s’adapter à de nouveaux défis globaux comme la crise climatique, les pandémies ou les migrations massives. Pour beaucoup, l’histoire jugera si cette réorganisation renforce vraiment la présence américaine dans le monde… ou si elle affaiblit au contraire, sa capacité à transformer des vies grâce à une aide humanitaire crédible et efficace.
Repenser
La disparition de l’Usaid conforte l’idée, de plus en
plus partagée sur le continent, que l’heure est venue de miser davantage sur
les ressources locales pour financer le développement. «L’aide ne peut plus
être considérée comme une solution fiable, ni durable. Le temps presse. Nous
devons agir maintenant, avec vous, nos chefs d’État, qui menez des réformes,
créez un environnement favorable et mobilisez les ressources nationales.
Ensemble, nous pouvons réaliser la promesse de l’Agenda 2063 et des Odd »,
affirmait récemment Claver Gatete, secrétaire exécutif de la Commission
économique pour l’Afrique, à l’occasion de la onzième session du Forum régional
africain pour le développement durable tenue à Kampala en Ouganda. 
Au Bénin, en Côte d’Ivoire ou au Sénégal, des voix s’élèvent pour rappeler qu’il faut renforcer la mobilisation des recettes fiscales, lutter contre l’évasion fiscale et développer des partenariats public-privé robustes. « Il faut faire des efforts de diversification des sources de financement en se tournant vers les marchés financiers régionaux et internationaux et vers les financements innovants. Les ressources les plus prévisibles et les plus durables sont les ressources publiques internes», indique Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, statisticien-économiste, spécialiste en gestion de la politique économique.
Pour plusieurs dirigeants africains, la multiplication des crises mondiales rend l’aide extérieure de plus en plus incertaine. La fin de l’Usaid pourrait être un déclic pour bâtir des systèmes plus résilients, adaptés aux réalités locales, tout en continuant à coopérer avec les bailleurs internationaux, mais sur des bases plus équilibrées.
a3747.en:
La Nation Bénin...

The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) officially ceased to exist this Tuesday, 1 July, after more than six decades of engagement in more than 100 countries. In sub-Saharan Africa, where several countries including Benin were among the main beneficiaries, this dissolution reshuffles the cards of cooperation and presents itself as a starting point for other, innovative financing systems.

It is a genuine turning point in the history of international cooperation. This Tuesday, 1 July, the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), a pillar of American humanitarian diplomacy since 1961, was officially dissolved, in accordance with a decision taken last March by the US Congress and endorsed by the White House. This marks the end of a model of development aid as it was built in the 20th century.

According to data from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), sub-Saharan Africa absorbed nearly 40% of USAID's annual budget. Countries such as Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, Senegal and Nigeria were among the main beneficiaries. In Benin, USAID financed structuring projects for access to drinking water, the fight against malaria and the strengthening of community health systems. In Togo, Burkina Faso, Nigeria and Senegal, several programmes transformed the daily lives of thousands of smallholder farmers and contributed to rural electrification. The support helped improve the education of young girls, climate resilience and local governance.

According to the White House, USAID's missions will henceforth be integrated directly into a Directorate-General for Cooperation and Development, attached to the US State Department. Officially, the aim is to streamline the structure, limit administrative duplication and strengthen the alignment between development aid and the diplomatic priorities of the United States. But this reorganisation raises questions about its concrete implementation.

The American embassies in each country will have to negotiate new continuity agreements with governments and local actors, in order to avoid an abrupt interruption of essential services.

Millions of people around the world benefited each year from USAID programmes, nearly a quarter of them in West Africa. The World Bank recalls that the agency was among the top five bilateral donors for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) related to health, education and gender equality. In practice, certain tripartite agreements have already been extended to 2026, notably in areas deemed strategic such as community health, education and food security. While the institution is expected to resume activities, the new directorate-general could take 12 to 18 months to become fully operational.

Motivations

On the American side, the dissolution is presented as a measure of sound management of public funds. A report by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) underlines that USAID managed more than 1,300 projects in 80 overseas missions, with duplication at times between federal agencies. The US administration defends a refocusing on major diplomatic priorities, in a context of heightened rivalry with China over investments in Africa and Asia. Yet several American officials find that USAID's strength lay precisely in its operational autonomy and its technical expertise. According to them, the technical expertise accumulated over the decades by USAID's teams could be diluted, or even lost, within a broader diplomatic apparatus where aid risks becoming a mere instrument of geopolitical influence.

After 63 years of existence, USAID leaves behind a legacy made of successes, whose actions are appreciated by populations. Its dissolution marks the end of a model, at a time when international cooperation must adapt to new global challenges such as the climate crisis, pandemics or mass migration. For many, history will judge whether this reorganisation really strengthens the American presence in the world... or whether, on the contrary, it weakens its capacity to transform lives through credible and effective humanitarian aid.

Rethinking

The disappearance of USAID reinforces the idea, increasingly shared across the continent, that the time has come to rely more on local resources to finance development. “Aid can no longer be considered a reliable or sustainable solution. Time is pressing. We must act now, with you, our heads of state, who are leading reforms, creating an enabling environment and mobilising domestic resources. Together, we can deliver on the promise of Agenda 2063 and the SDGs,” Claver Gatete, Executive Secretary of the Economic Commission for Africa, said recently at the eleventh session of the Africa Regional Forum on Sustainable Development held in Kampala, Uganda.

In Benin, Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal, voices are being raised to recall that it is necessary to strengthen the mobilisation of tax revenues, fight tax evasion and develop robust public-private partnerships. “Efforts must be made to diversify sources of financing by turning to regional and international financial markets and to innovative financing. The most predictable and most sustainable resources are domestic public resources,” says Epiphane Gilderic Adjovi, a statistician-economist and specialist in economic policy management.

For several African leaders, the multiplication of global crises makes external aid increasingly uncertain. The end of USAID could be a trigger for building more resilient systems, adapted to local realities, while continuing to cooperate with international donors, but on more balanced terms.
